answer: Final hypothesis (natural language): **The variable is SES (socioeconomic status).** In the supplied NLS data, the log-odds effect of SES on BA degree completion is significantly positive in the marginal (bivariate) model (+0.47, p<0.001) and remains positive after adjusting only for race (+0.35, near the stated +0.3636), but it decreases and crosses into negative territory (−0.23, near the stated −0.2293) once both race and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite and class percentile) are included in the logistic regression. The sign reversal is driven mainly by conditioning on the academic characteristics — SES is positively correlated with ability/class rank, and conditional on those resources higher-SES respondents complete BA degrees less often. Thus the marginal positive SES–BA association is a confounding artifact; the conditional association is negative. Every other candidate variable (ability, class percentile, family size, sex) keeps its sign across the same specifications, so SES is the only variable exhibiting the stated +0.36 → −0.23 pattern.
